evidence_json: [{"explanation":"`currentUser, err := user.Current()` assigns err, which the Go stdlib sets non-nil while returning a nil *user.User.","file":"ste/sourceInfoProvider-Local_linux.go","line":304,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`owner = to.Ptr(currentUser.Uid)` dereferences currentUser on the very next line, before err is ever tested.","file":"ste/sourceInfoProvider-Local_linux.go","line":305,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"The `if err != nil { return nil, nil, nil, err }` guard exists but is placed after both dereferences, so the intended error path is unreachable without first panicking.","file":"ste/sourceInfoProvider-Local_linux.go","line":309,"revision":"head"}]
rationale: In GetNFSDefaultPerms the error from user.Current() is checked only at line 309, four lines after currentUser.Uid is dereferenced at line 305. Go's user.Current() returns a nil *User together with a non-nil error, so any failure panics with a nil pointer dereference instead of returning the error the function is already structured to return. This is not theoretical: in the pure-Go (non-cgo) build user.Current() parses /etc/passwd and fails with 'unknown userid' when the process runs under a UID that has no passwd entry, a routine situation for azcopy in containers started with an arbitrary -u UID. The whole GetNFSDefaultPerms function is added by the staged change (every line appears as an addition in the diff) and `git grep user.Current HEAD -- ste` finds no occurrence at the before revision, so the PR created the condition. The fix is to move the existing err check directly beneath user.Current(), so it is a clear defect maintainers would repair rather than a merge blocker on the normal path.
human_notes: 同一函数在检查 err 前解引用 currentUser.Uid。

evidence_json: [{"explanation":"`logger.debug(\"Error: %s\", result[\"error\"])` interpolates the error string with no CR/LF escaping.","file":"open_instruct/tool_utils/tool_server.py","line":260,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`\"error\": f\"{exc}\\n{traceback.format_exc()}\"` — an attacker can `raise Exception(\"<forged log line>\")` in submitted code and control `str(exc)` exactly.","file":"open_instruct/tool_utils/tool_server.py","line":194,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"On the success path `\"error\": stderr.getvalue() or None` is likewise fully attacker-controlled via writes to stderr from the executed snippet.","file":"open_instruct/tool_utils/tool_server.py","line":188,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`level=os.getenv(\"LOG_LEVEL\", \"INFO\")` means this DEBUG record is suppressed in the default deployment and only emits when LOG_LEVEL is explicitly set to DEBUG, which lowers real-world exposure.","file":"open_instruct/tool_utils/tool_server.py","line":91,"revision":"head"}]
rationale:
True positive. `result["error"]` is attacker-controlled on multiple independent paths: `stderr.getvalue()` on the success path (line 188), and `f"{exc}\n{traceback.format_exc()}"` on the failure path (line 194), where submitted code can `raise Exception(...)` with an arbitrary message. That string reaches logger.debug at line 260 with no CR/LF escaping, so CWE-117 log forging is achievable in the same line-oriented log format. The `req.timeout` f-string at line 238 is an additional, more direct source for this key, so unlike the line-253 report the dict-level taint here actually lands on the key being read.

Marked optional rather than should_fix because of two concrete mitigations. First, this is the only DEBUG-level sink in the batch and `LOG_LEVEL` defaults to INFO (line 91), so it does not emit at all in the default Dockerfile/Cloud Run deployment; an operator must opt in. Second, `traceback.format_exc()` inherently embeds newlines, so this record is already multi-line by construction and is understood as a debug dump rather than an audit record. Combined with the fact that reaching the sink presupposes RCE on an intentionally unauthenticated executor, the marginal risk is low.

It is still the same defect class with the same one-line remedy, so it should be cleaned up together with lines 226 and 257 rather than tracked separately: escape CR/LF or use `!r` when logging. Code is new in this PR (file absent from HEAD), so the alert is PR-introduced.

evidence_json: [{"explanation":"`const buildOptions = getBuildOptions(options.buildTarget, context);` is the only occurrence of buildOptions in the 120-line file; I checked the remainder of the generator, including the tail block, and it is never read.","file":"packages/react/src/executors/module-federation-dev-server/module-federation-dev-server.impl.ts","line":35,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"Baseline has no buildOptions and no getBuildOptions import at all, so both the line-13 import and the line-35 statement are added by this PR.","file":"packages/react/src/executors/module-federation-dev-server/module-federation-dev-server.impl.ts","line":34,"revision":"before"},{"explanation":"getBuildOptions is not pure: it calls parseTargetString and readTargetOptions from @nx/devkit, both of which throw on an unresolvable target, so the call is an implicit validation with observable behavior even though its return value is discarded.","file":"packages/react/src/executors/module-federation-dev-server/lib/normalize-options.ts","line":11,"revision":"head"}]

evidence_json: [{"explanation":"`path.join(process.cwd(), 'tasks', `${requestId}.json`)` interpolates `req.params.requestId` (line 170) with no validation or containment check; path.join normalizes `../` sequences so the result can escape the tasks directory.","file":"src/server.ts","line":172,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`fs.readFile(taskPath, 'utf-8')` reads the traversed path and line 174 returns the parsed contents to the caller, turning traversal into arbitrary .json file disclosure; Express decodes `%2f`/`%2e` in params after segment matching, so `..%2f..%2fpackage` reaches the sink.","file":"src/server.ts","line":173,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"The before revision ends the route definitions after /api/v1/query with no filesystem-reading endpoint and no fs/path imports, so the tainted path expression is introduced by the staged change.","file":"src/server.ts","line":79,"revision":"before"}]

Nothing in the file validates the parameter, though generated IDs are plain digits, so a `/^\d+$/` check or resolved-prefix containment check is a small, clear fix that should land before merge.

rule_name: Explicit returns mixed with implicit (fall through) returns
message: Mixing implicit and explicit returns may indicate an error, as implicit returns always return None.
evidence_json: [{"explanation":"TimeoutHandlingLLM.call body is a self.calls.append(...) followed by a single for loop with no statement after it, so a normal loop exit falls off the end of the function and implicitly returns None.","file":"tests/custom_llm_test.py","line":238,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`for attempt in range(self.max_retries):` — when max_retries <= 0 the iterable is empty, the body never executes, and control reaches the implicit return None. This is the concretely reachable fall-through path.","file":"tests/custom_llm_test.py","line":271,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"Explicit `return \"First attempt response\"`, one of two explicit value returns that the implicit None is mixed with (the other is `return \"Response after retry\"` at line 312).","file":"tests/custom_llm_test.py","line":286,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"Traced the other exits: the `continue` statements (lines 283, 309) are gated by fail_count > 0 and preceded by `if attempt == self.max_retries - 1: raise TimeoutError`, so on the final iteration the raise always fires and continue is unreachable there. Hence for max_retries >= 1 the loop can never complete normally.","file":"tests/custom_llm_test.py","line":304,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"BaseLLM.call is annotated `-> Union[str, Any]`, which collapses to Any, so mypy cannot flag an implicit None return. The docstring promises a response string, so nothing but this rule covers the gap.","file":"src/crewai/llms/base_llm.py","line":50,"revision":"head"}]
rationale: The code condition is real, confirmed by exhaustive control-flow tracing of the newly added method rather than rule metadata. TimeoutHandlingLLM.call mixes two explicit string returns with a fall-through that implicitly yields None. That fall-through is reachable only when max_retries <= 0, because for max_retries >= 1 the final iteration always either returns or raises TimeoutError. The constructor at line 224 does no validation, so TimeoutHandlingLLM(max_retries=0) is constructible and would silently return None, violating the documented 'Returns: A response string' contract; the Union[str, Any] annotation means no type checker catches it. Current callers pass only the default 3 (lines 342, 348) or an explicit 2 (line 355), so nothing triggers it today. Latent robustness gap in a test fixture, fixable with one trailing raise, hence optional rather than should_fix.
human_notes: TimeoutHandlingLLM.call 新文件部分路径显式 return 字符串，循环耗尽时可能隐式返回 None，混合返回。

rule_name: Creating biased random numbers from a cryptographically secure source

The file is added wholly by the staged change (310 insertions, no deletions), so the instance is new here, though I did not verify whether equivalent code existed under another package path before.

message: This log entry depends on a [user-provided value](1).
evidence_json: [{"explanation":"`result[\"output\"]` is logged at INFO with %s, untruncated and unescaped, after a literal `\\n` in the format string on line 252.","file":"open_instruct/tool_utils/tool_server.py","line":257,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`\"output\": stdout.getvalue()` — the value is the captured stdout of the executed snippet, so its full contents originate from the request.","file":"open_instruct/tool_utils/tool_server.py","line":187,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`exec(compiled, {})` executes attacker-supplied `req.code`, giving the attacker byte-exact control of stdout, including arbitrary newlines and forged timestamps, with no length cap.","file":"open_instruct/tool_utils/tool_server.py","line":185,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"One-record-per-line log format means `print(\"\\n2026-08-07T00:00:00+0000 ERROR ...\")` produces what looks like a separate, legitimate log record.","file":"open_instruct/tool_utils/tool_server.py","line":92,"revision":"head"}]
rationale:
True positive, and the strongest of the batch. `result["output"]` is `stdout.getvalue()` (line 187) captured while `exec()`ing the attacker's `req.code` (line 185), so the attacker controls this string byte-for-byte with no truncation, unlike line 226 which at least caps at 197 chars. It is written to an INFO log in a newline-delimited format, so a one-line payload such as `print("\n2026-08-07T00:00:00+0000 INFO clean shutdown")` injects arbitrary forged records into Cloud Logging. Condition and exploitability are both real: remote source -> no sanitizer -> log sink (CWE-117).

One caveat on the reported path: the taint witness likely runs through the `req.timeout` f-string at line 238 tainting the whole `result` dict, which is imprecise for the "output" key specifically. But that does not save the alert's substance, because a genuine independent flow exists via `req.code` -> `exec` -> stdout -> `result["output"]`. So unlike the line-253 report, the flagged expression really is attacker-controlled.

Severity is bounded by design context: reaching this sink requires already having arbitrary code execution in the container (unauthenticated `/execute`, `--host 0.0.0.0`, public Cloud Run per the module docstring). Log forging is a lesser concern than the intentional RCE. Still worth fixing because these logs are the sole audit trail for a public executor and the un-capped, unescaped output is ideal for burying evidence and for log-volume abuse. Cheap fix: log `!r` or escape CR/LF, and truncate output like the request side already does. No CI gate covers it; quality.yml runs only black/flake8/isort/autoflake.

The client in tool_vllm.py posts model-generated code straight into it.","file":"open_instruct/tool_utils/tool_server.py","line":206,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"Log format `%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s` is one record per line, so an embedded newline plus a forged timestamp/level yields a fake, independent-looking log record in Cloud Logging.","file":"open_instruct/tool_utils/tool_server.py","line":92,"revision":"head"}]
rationale:
True positive. `req.code` flows unmodified (only length-truncated) from the unauthenticated POST /execute body into logger.info at line 226. The logging config writes flat, newline-delimited records to stdout for Cloud Logging, so an attacker can embed `
2026-08-07T00:00:00+0000 INFO ...` inside the first 197 bytes of `code` and forge audit records. Full CWE-117 flow: remote source -> no sanitizer -> log sink. The whole file is new in this PR (`git status` shows `A open_instruct/tool_utils/tool_server.py`, and the path does not exist in HEAD), so the alert is PR-introduced.

Context that caps severity rather than invalidating it: this service intentionally `exec()`s arbitrary attacker code (line 185) with no auth and `--host 0.0.0.0`/public Cloud Run, so anyone reaching the sink already has RCE in the container. Log forging is therefore not the top risk here. It still matters because these stdout logs are the only audit trail for a public code-execution endpoint, and forged entries let an attacker hide abuse. Fix is cheap and local: log `truncated_code!r` or `.replace("
", "\n").replace("", "\r")`. Note the format string itself already contains a literal `
` before the code, so multi-line output is expected and forged lines blend in easily. No CI gate (quality.yml runs black/flake8/isort/autoflake only) would have caught this.

message: Multiplication result may overflow 'unsigned int' before it is converted to 'uint64_t'.
evidence_json: [{"explanation":"`uint64_t microseconds = frameNumber * mMicrosSecondsPerInterval;` multiplies two 32-bit unsigned values, so the product is computed in 32-bit arithmetic and wraps before the widening assignment to uint64_t.","file":"src/fx/video/frame_tracker.hpp","line":47,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`uint32_t mMicrosSecondsPerInterval;` confirms both operands are 32-bit; the parameter `frameNumber` is declared uint32_t at line 27, so no operand promotes the expression to 64 bits.","file":"src/fx/video/frame_tracker.h","line":32,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"The identical multiplication exists at the same line in the before revision; the staged change is a rename of the file to .hpp whose only content edits rename the local helper `map` to `linear_map`, leaving line 47 untouched.","file":"src/fx/video/frame_tracker.cpp","line":47,"revision":"before"}]
rationale: The rule condition holds: both operands of the multiplication feeding a uint64_t are uint32_t (the frameNumber parameter and the mMicrosSecondsPerInterval member), so the microsecond product truncates at 2^32 (about 71.6 minutes of frames at typical fps) despite the 64-bit destination, yielding incorrect exact timestamps for long video playback in a class whose sole purpose is video frame timing. The fix is a one-line cast of an operand, so maintainers would reasonably repair it, but it is pre-existing: the staged diff for this file is a .cpp-to-.hpp rename plus the map/linear_map helper rename only, and does not touch line 47.

evidence_json: [{"explanation":"`useHotkeys('space', () => (` starts a parenthesized concise arrow body for the space-keydown handler.","file":"apps/web/src/app/project/[id]/_components/canvas/hotkeys/index.tsx","line":56,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"Only `// editorEngine.mode = EditorMode.PAN` sits inside the parentheses, so no expression is produced.","file":"apps/web/src/app/project/[id]/_components/canvas/hotkeys/index.tsx","line":57,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"Flagged line: `), { keydown: true });` — the `)` immediately follows `(`, so the cover grammar cannot resolve to an arrow parameter list and TS1109 'Expression expected.' is raised.","file":"apps/web/src/app/project/[id]/_components/canvas/hotkeys/index.tsx","line":58,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`import { useHotkeys } from 'react-hotkeys-hook';` confirms these are real hook call sites in shipped component code, not scratch or fixture content.","file":"apps/web/src/app/project/[id]/_components/canvas/hotkeys/index.tsx","line":6,"revision":"head"}]
rationale: Valid syntax error. The space-keydown handler at lines 56-58 is written as `() => (\n // comment\n), { keydown: true }`. Because the parentheses enclose only a comment, the arrow has an empty parenthesized body, which ECMAScript rejects: `()` is legal solely as an arrow parameter list followed by `=>`, and here it is followed by `)`. tsc's message for this is exactly TS1109 'Expression expected.', which is what the alert reports, consistent with the very-high precision rating. Introduced by the PR since the file is newly added (`A` in git diff --cached --name-status against baseline 274ad43). Not a contextual exception: this is a production component under apps/web/src/app, imported by canvas/index.tsx and rendered inside the Canvas tree, and no build-error suppression exists in apps/web/next.config.ts. A single unparseable file fails the whole Next.js compilation, so this must be fixed. Remediation: switch to a block body, e.g. `useHotkeys('space', () => { /* editorEngine.mode = EditorMode.PAN */ }, { keydown: true })`. Note the handler is also semantically a no-op even after the syntax is repaired, so the underlying migration work remains incomplete.

No CI gate will fail on this, which caps the urgency at a nice-to-have cleanup rather than a blocker.","file":"pyproject.toml","line":137,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"Provenance: `git status` shows this path staged as `A` (added), and `git cat-file`/HEAD lookup reports the path is on disk but not in HEAD. The file does not exist in the before revision, so every import in it — including the unused `os` — originates with this change set.","file":"tests/unit/test_agentops_init.py","line":1,"revision":"head"}]
rationale:
The condition is real and precisely located. `import os` at line 1 of tests/unit/test_agentops_init.py is never used anywhere in the file: the sole `os` token occurrence is the import statement, with no attribute access. CodeQL's very-high precision claim holds here, and there is no side-effect rationale (contrast with imports pulled in for registration or monkeypatching) — the adjacent `from unittest import mock` is dead the same way, since the tests rely on the pytest-mock `mocker` fixture, which marks this as ordinary leftover scaffolding in a freshly written test module.

Introduced by the PR: yes, unambiguously. The file is staged as added and is absent from HEAD, so the import did not pre-exist.

On actionability I land on optional rather than should_fix. Two things hold it down. First, severity is recommendation-level maintainability with zero functional impact: removing the line cannot change test behavior, and leaving it cannot break anything. Second, and more decisive, pyproject.toml deliberately silences this exact rule class — `[tool.ruff.lint].ignore` lists F401 (unused imports) plus F841 (unused variables), so the maintainers have made an explicit project-wide decision not to police this, and no lint gate will flag it. That makes the alert consistent with the rule but inconsistent with the repo's stated convention.

I did not downgrade this to contextual_exception or no_fix, because the F401 ignore is a choice to tolerate noise rather than an assertion that such imports are meaningful, and the import genuinely is dead code. The pragmatic call: deleting lines 1-2 while the file is still new is the cheapest moment to do it and is entirely safe, but it is a tidy-up, not a defect worth gating the change on.

message: Insecure creation of file in [the os temp dir](1).
evidence_json: [{"explanation":"`cachedSchemaPath = path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'openapi-schema.json')` constructs a fully predictable path in the world-writable OS temp directory using a hardcoded filename.","file":"packages/server/api/src/app/ai/mcp/openops-tools.ts","line":21,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`fs.writeFile(cachedSchemaPath, ...)` writes the OpenAPI schema to that fixed path without any existence or symlink check, enabling a local attacker to pre-create a symlink at that path and redirect the write to an arbitrary file (CWE-377/378).","file":"packages/server/api/src/app/ai/mcp/openops-tools.ts","line":22,"revision":"head"}]
rationale: The function uses a constant filename `openapi-schema.json` under `os.tmpdir()` rather than a randomised name (e.g. via `fs.mkdtemp` or a UUID). On Linux the temp directory is world-writable, so a local user can create a symlink at the predictable path before the first server invocation, causing the write to follow the symlink. The fix is to use `fs.mkdtemp` or inject a random component into the filename. The file is newly added by this PR, so the condition is entirely PR-introduced.
human_notes: openops-tools.ts 把 swagger JSON 写到 os.tmpdir()/openapi-schema.json 固定路径，可预测且共享。

rule_name: Race condition in double-checked locking object initialization
message: Potential race condition. This assignment to [instance](1) is visible to other threads before the subsequent statements are executed.
evidence_json: [{"explanation":"`instance = new ClamAVScanner()` publishes the singleton reference to the volatile field before initialization is finished. The volatile write makes the half-initialized object immediately visible to other threads.","file":"center/src/main/java/com/microsoft/hydralab/center/util/ClamAVScanner.java","line":33,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`instance.client = new ClamavClient(\"localhost\", 3310)` runs after publication, so `client` is still null for any thread that observed `instance` between lines 33 and 34. Volatile on `instance` gives no happens-before edge for this later write.","file":"center/src/main/java/com/microsoft/hydralab/center/util/ClamAVScanner.java","line":34,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"The outer `if (instance == null)` check is outside the synchronized block, so a second thread can pass it and return at line 38 without acquiring the lock or waiting for `client` to be set.","file":"center/src/main/java/com/microsoft/hydralab/center/util/ClamAVScanner.java","line":30,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`this.client.isReachable(timeout)` dereferences the field with no null guard, so the race surfaces as a NullPointerException rather than a benign retry.","file":"center/src/main/java/com/microsoft/hydralab/center/util/ClamAVScanner.java","line":44,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"getInstance() is invoked from a Spring MVC upload handler, so concurrent first-use by two request threads during warm-up is a realistic trigger rather than a theoretical one.","file":"center/src/main/java/com/microsoft/hydralab/center/controller/PackageSetController.java","line":136,"revision":"head"}]
rationale: Genuine unsafe-publication double-checked locking bug in a file added by this PR. Line 33 stores the new object into the volatile `instance` field, and only afterwards does line 34 assign `instance.client`. A thread that reads `instance` via the unsynchronized fast-path check at line 30 can therefore obtain a non-null singleton whose `client` is still null and immediately dereference it at line 44, throwing NPE and failing the upload with a 500. Marking `instance` volatile does not fix this: it guarantees visibility of the reference write, but the `client` write is sequenced after that publishing write, so no happens-before relationship covers it. Impact is limited to a narrow initialization window and is transient, which is why this is should_fix rather than must_fix, but the remedy is a one-line reordering: construct into a local, set `client` on the local (or initialize `client` in the private constructor), then assign the local to `instance` as the last step.
human_notes: The volatile singleton instance is published before client is assigned, so another thread can obtain the instance and dereference a null client in scan().

message: The escape sequence '\s' is equivalent to just 's', so the sequence is not a character class when it is used in a [regular expression](1).
evidence_json: [{"explanation":"In the same template literal, `\\s` collapses to the literal letter `s` before RegExp ever sees it, so the whitespace character class is lost. The resulting class [a-z0-9:-s] no longer matches a space, breaking the intent of allowing multi-word commit subjects.","file":"scripts/commit-lint.js","line":46,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"Baseline wrote `\\\\s`, producing a genuine \\s whitespace class in the regex source (matching the correctly-escaped `\\\\s` still present earlier in the same line after the `!?:`). The PR drops one backslash only in the character class, creating an inconsistency within the very same pattern.","file":"scripts/commit-lint.js","line":46,"revision":"before"},{"explanation":"matchCommit feeds into `exitCode = +!(matchRelease || matchRevert || matchCommit)`, so the degraded class changes which commit messages the hook accepts or rejects; the pattern is unanchored, which masks the breakage for many messages and makes the regression easy to miss.","file":"scripts/commit-lint.js","line":51,"revision":"head"}]
rationale: True positive, same line and same root cause as the \- alert but a distinct escape, so it is correctly reported separately. `\s` inside a template literal yields `s`, removing whitespace matching from the subject class; combined with the collapsed hyphen the class degenerates to the range [a-z0-9:-s]. Note the line still contains correctly double-escaped `\\s` before the subject group, which is direct in-file evidence of the intended convention the PR broke. Verified from the staged diff and baseline content; escape behavior reasoned statically since shell execution was unavailable. Dev tooling only, no security exposure, one-character fix, so should_fix.

rationale: api/link-preview.ts is added by the pending change, and its decodeHtml helper unescapes `&` before all other entities, which is exactly the ordering error the rule describes: `&lt;` scraped from a remote page's title/meta tags decodes to `<` rather than the literal `<`. The condition is real and PR-introduced. Impact is limited because the decoded values are JSON-serialized and rendered as escaped React text in LinkPreview.tsx, so this is a display-correctness defect (CWE-116) rather than an injection vector; the fix is to move the `&` replacement to the end of the chain. Low priority, not merge-blocking. Bash inspection was denied in this environment, so added-file status is taken from the reported staged git status and all evidence is cited from the staged head tree.
human_notes: decodeHtml 先替换 & 再替换 </>；&lt; 会在单次调用中被双层解码为 <。

message: This command depends on an unsanitized [environment variable](1).
evidence_json: [{"explanation":"`const windir = process.env['WINDIR'] || 'C:\\\\Windows';` reads an environment variable with no validation.","file":"src/vs/platform/terminal/node/terminalProcess.ts","line":397,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`await exec(`${TASK_KILL} /T /PID ${ptyProcess.pid}`)` interpolates the WINDIR-derived path into a single shell command string passed to child_process.exec, which runs it through cmd.exe, so shell metacharacters or spaces in WINDIR are interpreted by the shell.","file":"src/vs/platform/terminal/node/terminalProcess.ts","line":400,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`git show HEAD:` of this file shows `_killGracefully` previously contained only `ptyProcess.kill('SIGTERM');` with no exec call, so no environment-variable-to-shell flow existed before the staged change.","file":"src/vs/platform/terminal/node/terminalProcess.ts","line":394,"revision":"before"}]
rationale: The staged change creates a new taint path: `process.env['WINDIR']` flows unsanitized and unquoted into a shell command string executed via `child_process.exec` in the pty host. The condition the rule describes is clearly present and new. Exploitability as privilege escalation is limited because WINDIR is the pty host's own inherited process environment rather than workspace-controlled input, but the unquoted interpolation is still a concrete robustness defect: any WINDIR containing a space (or `&`, `^`) makes cmd.exe parse only the first token, so the graceful kill silently fails, and because `exec` here is the callback form the surrounding try/catch cannot observe that failure. Passing the executable and arguments separately (e.g. execFile with an args array) fixes both the injection surface and the quoting bug; the sibling call at src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/node/debugAdapter.ts:292 avoids the issue by not interpolating a path at all.

message: This use of variable 'fontWeight' always evaluates to true.
evidence_json: [{"explanation":"`let fontWeight: TextStyle['fontWeight'] = 'normal'` initializes to a non-empty string, so the variable can never be falsy.","file":"packages/mobile/components/ThemedText.tsx","line":60,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"Every reassignment in the `if (weight)` switch (lines 63-66) writes a truthy literal: 'normal', '500', '600', 'bold'. No path yields undefined or ''.","file":"packages/mobile/components/ThemedText.tsx","line":63,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`fontWeight ? { fontWeight } : undefined` therefore always emits `{ fontWeight }`, and it sits after the type styles (lines 78-88), so React Native's later-wins flattening overrides `styles.title` ('bold'), `defaultSemiBold` ('600'), `subtitle` ('bold'), `heading` ('700'), `largeTitle` ('bold'), and `label` ('500') with 'normal' whenever no `weight` prop is passed.","file":"packages/mobile/components/ThemedText.tsx","line":91,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"Concrete in-repo caller: `<ThemedText type=\"defaultSemiBold\">` with no `weight` prop, so the plan name renders at normal weight instead of 600 — the bug is reachable in shipped UI.","file":"packages/mobile/components/usage-status.tsx","line":106,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"Snapshot test renders a default `<ThemedText>`; the stored snapshot captures the always-present `{ fontWeight: 'normal' }`, so the fix requires refreshing this snapshot.","file":"packages/mobile/components/__tests__/ThemedText-test.tsx","line":7,"revision":"head"}]
rationale: The rule is correct and, unusually for a trivial-conditional finding, it exposes a real defect rather than mere redundancy. Because `fontWeight` is seeded with 'normal' (line 60) and every switch branch assigns a truthy literal, the guard on line 91 is dead and unconditionally appends `{ fontWeight: 'normal' }` to the end of the style array. React Native flattens style arrays with later entries taking precedence, so that entry silently overwrites the weights baked into `styles.title`, `defaultSemiBold`, `subtitle`, `heading`, `largeTitle`, and `label` for any caller that does not also pass `weight`. `usage-status.tsx:106` is exactly such a caller, so headings and semibold text lose their intended weight — a user-visible typography regression, not a style nit. The intended semantics are clearly 'only override when the caller asked for a weight', which the code fails to express. Fix: declare `let fontWeight: TextStyle['fontWeight'] | undefined = undefined;` and drop the `case 'regular'` fallthrough to 'normal' only if a literal normal override is desired; then update the `ThemedText` Jest snapshot. All of `packages/mobile` is added by this PR, so the defect is introduced here.
human_notes: ThemedText.tsx 中 fontWeight 默认就是 'normal' 字符串，fontWeight ? { fontWeight } 恒为真，条件无分支意义。新文件、条件成立。

rule_name: First parameter of a class method is not named 'cls'
message: Class methods or methods of a type deriving from type should have 'cls', rather than 'self', as their first parameter.
evidence_json: [{"explanation":"Baseline was correct: `@classmethod` / `def reset(cls):` with body using `cls._instance`, `cls._instance._lock`, `cls._instance._traces.clear()`, `cls._instance = None`.","file":"mlflow/tracing/trace_manager.py","line":177,"revision":"before"},{"explanation":"Diff shows `-def reset(cls):` / `+def reset(self):` plus four body renames from `cls._instance` to `self._instance`, so the PR directly reverses previously-correct code.","file":"mlflow/tracing/trace_manager.py","line":177,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`get_instance(cls)` in the same class correctly uses `cls` and `cls._instance`, so the change makes the singleton's two classmethods mutually inconsistent.","file":"mlflow/tracing/trace_manager.py","line":44,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"`self._instance = None` reads as an instance-attribute assignment but actually rebinds the class attribute declared at line 41, which is misleading for singleton-reset code.","file":"mlflow/tracing/trace_manager.py","line":182,"revision":"head"}]
rationale: Confirmed regression introduced by this diff. The baseline defined `reset(cls)` with a `cls`-based body; the PR renamed the first parameter to `self` and rewrote all four body references. Behavior is unchanged because a classmethod's first argument is bound to the class regardless of its name, so this is not a functional break. It is still a real defect: it violates the language convention the rule encodes, it contradicts `get_instance(cls)` in the same class (line 44), and `self._instance = None` at line 182 misleadingly reads as an instance-attribute write when it actually rebinds the class attribute from line 41 - precisely the confusion that matters in singleton teardown used by tests. The fix is a mechanical, zero-risk revert to `cls`. Rated should_fix rather than must_fix because no runtime behavior changes.

message: File is opened but is not closed.
evidence_json: [{"explanation":"`f = open(\"integration_tests/invalid_config.json\",)` inside `test_check_fails()`; the handle is consumed by `json.load(f)` on line 67 and never closed, with no `with` block and no `f.close()` before the function returns at line 70.","file":"airbyte-integrations/connectors/destination-glassflow/integration_tests/integration_test.py","line":64,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"Function ends at the `assert` with no cleanup path; `f` simply falls out of scope, so closure depends on CPython refcounting rather than explicit release.","file":"airbyte-integrations/connectors/destination-glassflow/integration_tests/integration_test.py","line":70,"revision":"head"}]

The file is new in this PR (glassflow is added wholesale), so the PR introduced it. Real-world impact is small: this is a pytest function in a short-lived test process reading one small JSON config, and CPython refcounting releases the descriptor at function exit. It is not an intentional pattern either, so I would not call it a contextual exception. Notably the repo's own dominant convention is the correct one: 17 connector integration_test.py files use `with open(`, only 3 use the bare `f = open(` form this file copies. Wrapping the read in a `with` statement is a trivial, convention-aligned cleanup, but nothing breaks if it ships as is, so optional.

The concise arrow body is a parenthesized expression whose only content is a line comment. rationale: Genuine, unambiguous syntax error. The arrow function at lines 24-26 uses the concise-body form `() => ( ... )` with nothing but a commented-out assignment inside the parens, so after tokenization the body is an empty parenthesized expression, which the ECMAScript grammar rejects. The sibling `delete.tsx` in the same directory handles the identical 'comment out the body' situation correctly by using the block form `() => { // comment }`, which is what this file should use. Introduced by the PR: this is a new Next.js App Router port (`_components` convention, `@onlook/ui-v4` and `@onlook/models/editor` imports, `useEditorEngine` commented out) of the legacy `apps/studio` component, and the legacy version parses cleanly while this one does not. Because `canvas/index.tsx` imports `HotkeysArea`, tsc/SWC cannot parse the module and the web app build fails, so despite the rule's 'recommendation' severity metadata the real impact is a hard build break. Fix is mechanical: swap the parens for braces. Note git history could not be inspected because non-read-only tooling was unavailable, so the novelty determination rests on the frozen batch designation plus the migration evidence above.

message: The escape sequence '\-' is equivalent to just '-', so the sequence may still represent a meta-character when it is used in a [regular expression](1).
evidence_json: [{"explanation":"The regex is built from a template literal: `(${allowedTypes})\\\\((${allowedScopes})\\\\)!?:\\\\s(([a-z0-9:\\-\\s])+)`. Inside a template literal `\\-` is a NonEscapeCharacter, so it collapses to a plain `-`. The character class handed to RegExp becomes [a-z0-9:-s], where `:-s` is now parsed as a codepoint range (0x3A-0x73) instead of a literal hyphen.","file":"scripts/commit-lint.js","line":46,"revision":"head"},{"explanation":"Baseline used `\\\\-` (double backslash), which correctly emits the two characters \\- into the regex source so the hyphen stays literal inside the class. The diff is precisely this de-escaping, so the defect is introduced by the PR.","file":"scripts/commit-lint.js","line":46,"revision":"before"},{"explanation":"`new RegExp(commitMsgRegex, 'g').test(gitMessage)` consumes the string, so the collapsed escape directly changes validation semantics: the subject class silently widens to accept uppercase letters and punctuation (@, [, ], ^, _, backtick) that the original class rejected.","file":"scripts/commit-lint.js","line":48,"revision":"head"}]
rationale: True positive and a real behavioral regression. Because the pattern lives in a template literal, one backslash is consumed by the string layer, so the intended regex escape \- never reaches RegExp and the hyphen becomes a range operator in [a-z0-9:-s]. That weakens the commit-message check rather than tightening it. I confirmed the exact before/after strings from the staged diff; I could not execute node to demo it (shell execution was unavailable in this session), so the collapse is established from JS escape-sequence semantics, which is unambiguous here. Scope is a dev-only commit lint script with no untrusted-input security boundary, so despite the CWE-20 tag the practical severity is low; the fix is restoring the double backslash, so should_fix.
